newsitem.title: JAPAN: Excessive forex moves should be avoided--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Excessive forex moves should be avoided--MOF.

text.p: Excessive changes in currency rates should be avoided, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday.
He added that the most important thing for any currency is that it is in balance with real economic conditions.
"The most important thing for any country's currency is that it is in balance with the economy, not about specific levels. Currencies should also avoid rapid changes as much as possible," he said.

Ogawa said he would like to wait for the outcome of Sunday's meeting in Washington of the Group of Seven (G7) nations, which he said is likely to discuss stability in foreign exchange markets and whether currencies are in line with fundamentals.

Asked about a report by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Thursday saying Japan should continue its easy monetary policy until an autonomous recovery is established, Ogawa said: "We do not feel out of step with the stance taken by the Bank of Japan governor."
BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday that the central bank's monetary policy would put emphasis on strengthening the basis for economic recovery.
Ogawa said the Japanese economy was become firmer, centring on domestic demand, compared with early last year.
"Currently the economic cycle is at a place where it is good and firm," he said.
He also said he expects such firmness to continue. For it to do so, it was important for Japan to carry out various planned economic reforms.
The outlook for the global economy outlined in the IMF report was generally in line with Japan's view, he said.
